py02.title: Count API responses
py02.goal: Count how often each status code appears.
py02.teaching:
A dictionary maps a **key** to its current **count**. The first time a key appears, its count starts at zero. Each later occurrence updates that same entry.

> [!WARNING]
> Do not reset the whole dictionary inside the loop. Keep the accumulated counts across iterations.
py02.task: `count_statuses(codes)` returns a dictionary mapping each integer status code to its count. Do not change the input.
py02.reflection: Can your loop handle a key it has never seen before? What should an empty input return?

py03.title: Deduplicate job IDs
py03.goal: Remove duplicate IDs while preserving their first-seen order.
py03.teaching:
A **set** answers whether a value has appeared before. A **list** preserves the order you choose. Combining them lets you keep the first occurrence of each value without sorting the input.

> [!WARNING]
> Converting directly to a set removes duplicates but does not express the required first-seen order.
py03.task: `unique_jobs(ids)` returns the first occurrence of each string, preserving input order. IDs are case sensitive. Leave the input unchanged.
py03.reflection: Which operation records that an item has been seen? Which operation preserves its original position?

py05.title: Validate configuration
py05.goal: Validate port text, then convert it to an integer.
py05.teaching:
Configuration arrives as text. **Normalization**, **validation**, and **conversion** are separate steps. Stripping surrounding whitespace can be acceptable even when spaces inside a number are not.

> [!WARNING]
> A conversion succeeding does not prove the value meets your application rules. Check the range as well.
py05.example:
raw = " 42 "
cleaned = raw.strip()
if not cleaned.isascii() or not cleaned.isdecimal():
    raise ValueError("Expected decimal digits")
value = int(cleaned)
py05.task: `parse_port(text)` accepts a string of ASCII digits, optionally surrounded by whitespace, and returns an integer from 1 to 65535. Raise `ValueError` for signs, non-digits, empty strings, and out-of-range values.
py05.reflection: Which inputs should be accepted? Decide what empty text, signs, decimals, and out-of-range values mean before writing the conversion.

py07.title: Typed task records
py07.goal: Validate incoming values and construct a clean task record.
py07.teaching:
A type annotation documents an expected shape, but it does **not validate runtime input**. Check the values you received before constructing a clean record for the rest of your application.

> [!WARNING]
> Do not use bool(value) as a substitute for validating a boolean. The string "false" is truthy.
py07.task: `normalize_task(data)` returns a fresh dictionary with exactly `title` (stripped nonempty string) and `done` (boolean, defaults to False). Reject invalid titles or nonboolean done values with `ValueError`. Ignore extra fields. Add type hints.
py07.reflection: Which fields may be normalized, and which must already have the correct type?

py04.title: Scope and pure functions
py04.goal: Apply a discount without changing the original prices.
py04.teaching:
A function call has its own **local variables**. Assigning a new local name does not change a global name. A **pure transformation** returns a new value and leaves the input collection unchanged.

> [!WARNING]
> Changing prices in place creates a side effect. Validate the percentage before building the result.
py04.example:
def add_fee(amounts, fee):
    return [amount + fee for amount in amounts]

original = [10, 20]
updated = add_fee(original, 3)
# original remains [10, 20]
py04.task: `apply_discount(prices, percent)` returns a new list of integer prices using `price * (100-percent) // 100`. Reject percentages outside 0..100. Never mutate `prices` or `DEFAULT_PRICES`.
py04.reflection: If two names refer to the same list, what happens when one name changes an element? How does building a new list avoid that?

py01.title: Invoice totals
py01.goal: Calculate an invoice total using integer cents.
py01.teaching:
Represent money as **integer cents** so ordinary arithmetic stays exact. An accumulator starts with the identity for the operation: **zero** for addition. Each loop iteration contributes one line item.

> [!WARNING]
> Validate both values in a pair. A negative quantity is just as invalid as a negative price.
py01.example:
subtotal = 0
for amount in [125, 250, 75]:
    subtotal += amount
print(subtotal)  # 450
py01.task: `invoice_total(items)` receives `(unit_price_cents, quantity)` pairs. Return their total. Reject negative prices or quantities with `ValueError`; an empty invoice costs zero.
py01.reflection: What should an empty collection contribute? Where should invalid input be rejected?

py06.title: Paginate query results
py06.goal: Return one page of items using a new list slice.
py06.teaching:
Page numbers are usually **one-based** while list indices are **zero-based**. Convert the page once, then use slicing. Python slices naturally return fewer items at the end of a collection.

> [!WARNING]
> In Python, bool is a subclass of int. Reject booleans explicitly when the contract requires an actual integer.
py06.example:
items = ["a", "b", "c", "d", "e"]
start = 2
size = 2
window = items[start:start + size]  # ["c", "d"]
py06.task: `paginate(items, page, size)` returns one page as a new list. Page and size must be positive integers; reject booleans and other types with `ValueError`. A page beyond the end returns `[]`.
py06.reflection: Where does page one start? What should happen when the requested page begins beyond the last item?

py08.title: A FIFO job queue
py08.goal: Build a queue that serves the oldest job first.
py08.teaching:
A queue follows **first in, first out**. Each queue object needs its own storage. Initialize mutable state inside the constructor so two objects do not accidentally share jobs.

> [!WARNING]
> A mutable class attribute is shared by instances. Put per-queue storage on self in __init__.
py08.example:
class Mailbox:
    def __init__(self):
        self.messages = []

first = Mailbox()
second = Mailbox()
first.messages.append("hello")
# second.messages is still empty
py08.task: Implement `JobQueue`: `push(job)` appends any value, `pop()` removes and returns the oldest, `len(queue)` counts items. Empty pop raises `IndexError`. Instances must not share storage. Prefer collections.deque.
py08.reflection: Which end receives new jobs? Which end removes the oldest one? What is the empty-queue contract?

py09.title: Functional log aggregation
py09.goal: Filter successful events and add their amounts.
py09.teaching:
Separate a data pipeline into three questions: **which records qualify**, **what value each produces**, and **how those values combine**. A generator can pass one value at a time into an aggregation.

> [!WARNING]
> Do not mutate the input while aggregating. Keep filtering decisions distinct from output construction.
py09.example:
events = [{"ok": True, "ms": 12}, {"ok": False, "ms": 90}]
total = sum(event["ms"] for event in events if event["ok"])
# 12
py09.task: `sum_successful(events)` sums `amount` for event dictionaries whose `status` equals `"ok"`. Skip other statuses and missing status values. Successful events always have numeric amounts. Do not mutate the input.
py09.reflection: Can the input be consumed only once? Are you changing any record while reading it?

py10.title: Binary search
py10.goal: Find a target by repeatedly halving a sorted search interval.
py10.teaching:
**Binary search** relies on sorted input. After inspecting the middle value, discard the half that cannot contain the target. Every unsuccessful iteration must make the remaining interval smaller.

> [!WARNING]
> Move a bound past the inspected middle position. Keeping the same middle can create an infinite loop.
py10.example:
values = [3, 8, 14, 21, 30]
left, right = 0, len(values) - 1
middle = (left + right) // 2
# values[middle] is 14
py10.task: `find_index(values, target)` returns an index containing target, or -1 when absent. Any matching index is acceptable for duplicates. Use binary search rather than list.index or a linear loop.
py10.reflection: What invariant describes the remaining search interval? When does an empty interval mean the target is absent?

py11.title: SQLite task storage
py11.goal: Store and list tasks using parameterized SQLite queries.
py11.teaching:
SQL text describes a query. **Parameters** carry user data separately. This preserves literal characters in titles and avoids interpreting a value as part of the SQL program.

> [!WARNING]
> A one-element tuple needs a trailing comma. Never interpolate a title into an SQL statement.
py11.example:
cursor = connection.execute(
    "SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = ?",
    (user_id,),
)
row = cursor.fetchone()
py11.task: Implement `create_schema(conn)`, `add_task(conn, title)` returning the integer id, and `list_tasks(conn)` returning `(id, title)` tuples in id order. Schema: tasks(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL). Strip titles and reject empty ones. Commit writes. Use SQL parameters.
py11.reflection: How will quotes in a title be handled? What result should a missing row produce?

py12.title: Cache expiry
py12.goal: Keep cached values valid only until their expiry time.
py12.teaching:
An expiring cache needs both a **stored value** and an **expiry time**. Expiration is a comparison against the current clock. A cached zero, False, or empty string can still be a valid hit.

> [!WARNING]
> Do not use truthiness to decide whether a key exists. Check membership and expiry separately.
py12.example:
now = 100
ttl = 10
entry = {"value": 0, "expires_at": now + ttl}
expired = 110 >= entry["expires_at"]  # True
py12.task: Implement `Cache`: `set(key, value, ttl, now)` stores a value with deadline now+ttl; negative TTL raises ValueError. `get(key, now)` returns the stored value if now is before deadline, otherwise None. Overwrites replace the deadline. Each instance is independent.
py12.reflection: Is an entry valid exactly at its deadline? Can your tests control the clock?
